about: A 6 x 6 in sine plate (McMaster 5216A24 class) set at 10 deg on a wrung gauge-block stack (0.750 + 0.100 + 0.018 = 0.868 in = 5 sin 10 deg), modelled from scratch in the placeholder's frame: ground base and top plate 3/4 in thick, the top's 4 x 4 grid of 3/8-16 tapped holes at 1-1/4 in, a ground end stop on two socket-head screws at its low end, both 1/2 in rolls in clamp blocks under the top plate 5 in apart, the hinge roll cradled in two knuckle blocks on the base; the stack's blocks lapped, the .750 etched.
reviewed: 2026-11-05: draft; the geometry reproduces the placeholder's box to 0.2 mm (its stack, 15.7 mm tall, is made the 22.05 mm the angle needs)

sine_tapped.about: the tapped holes' threaded walls: cut, unground, catching little light

sine_lapped.about: lapped gauge-block steel: a near mirror

unsure.what: no side locking clamps: they would stand ~10 mm proud of the record's box; plain sine plates without them exist
the placeholder's gauge stack (15.7 mm) can't hold the roll at 10 deg; the model's is the 22.05 mm stack the angle needs
